text.p: Here are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade University Rector Dragutin Velickovic proposes dismissal of 13 deans who supported the student protest and says he will resign when the students return to classes.
- Belgrade university teaching board will decide today together with the students on whether classes will resume.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno has prepared a proposal for dialogue on conditions of democratic elections which should start by March 20 the latest.
- The Yugoslav Left and the Socialist Party of Serbia confirm the unity of left forces in Serbia and announce they will run jointly in Serbia's parliamentary elections to be held later this year.
- Serbian teachers suspend strike without their demands having been met and vow to resume it if wages are not paid out regularly or reprercussions are taken against any of the striking teachers.
- President of the Moslem-Croat federation Kresimir Zubak and Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic discuss in Banja Luka release of prisoners of war and economic cooperation.
- Zastava Cars from Kragujevac still choosing its future partner, representatives of Korea's Hyundai to visit factory in the next few days. France's Peugeot mentioned as the other potential partner.
- Serbia's electricity company EPS to increase prices "slightly" in order to be able to carry out the necessary rehauling, says deputy director Novica Maskovic.
- President of Serbian Chamber of Economy Vlajko Stojiljkovic asks Serbian PTT to reexamine its telephone price increase.
POLITIKA
- High-level Roman Catholic Franciscan delegation to make a three-day visit Serbian Orthodox Church starting March 21.
- Yugoslav ambassador in U.N. calls on the organisation to urge Croatian government to secure necessary conditions for holding elections in Eastern Slavonia.
- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia to set up their party - The Atunomous Democratic Serb Party (SDSS) in Borovo Naselje.
- Truck factory from Priboj FAP accuses Zastava trucks of directly taking over its production programme with its announced deal with Italian Iveco.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia preparing to close five more banks of the 105 officially operating in the country.
- Serbian education minister Jovo Todorovic announces education reforms and and preparation of new University law.
- Nineteen of 28 NIN weekly journalists informed the newly- apppointed director of the magazine Tomislav Dzadzic they were going on strike.
- Serbian Renewal Movement forms committee for restoration of monarchy.
- Serb representative in Bosnia's Presidency Momcilo Krajisnik says the agreement between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic is useful for the Serb people.
- Preschool employees continue strike following failed talks in the municipal assembly.

- Scores of students crash reception for foreign and domestic jouranlists organised by new Serbian Information minister Radmila Milentijevic. The minister says this shows existence of freedom in Serbia and calls on everyone to work.
BLIC
- ICN-Yugoslavia has extended a $50 million dollar one-year credit to Serbia to normalise supply of medicines.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Several international firms interested in joint oil exploration in Montenegro with Jugopetrol of Kotor, among them Occidental from the United States.

- Gradina crossing on Yugoslav-Bulgarian border a trap for drug smugglers. Last year Yugoslav border officials seized more than 500 kilograms of heroin with a street value of nearly 50 million German marks according to Belgrade prices.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Media first target of new opposition authorities in Serbian towns where they won a majority in local elections. Cooperation with Radio Television Serbia severed, mass replacements of editors and journalists. In Kragujevac, 42 journalists listed as "unsuitable".
- New credit arrangements between Serbian Health Insurance Fund and Yugoslav pharmaceutical companies and their commercial banks to ease medicine shortages on the market.
